# Finn Ole Semrau

I study how **global value chains and foreign direct investment** shape firms’ environmental performance, and how governments design **industrial policy** to scale green technologies in the face of international competition and geopolitical pressure.

## About

::: {.about-grid}

::: {.about-photo}

![](images/finn-semrau.jpg)

:::

::: {.about-text}

I am an economist and postdoctoral researcher at the [Kiel Institute for the World Economy](https://www.kielinstitut.de/de/expertinnen-und-experten/finn-ole-semrau/){.inline-link}, where I serve as Deputy Scientific Lead of the [Industrial Policy Lab](https://industrialpolicylab.de/de/start/){.inline-link}. I am also an Add-on Fellow of the [Joachim Herz Foundation](https://www.joachim-herz-stiftung.de/){.inline-link} (2026–2028).

My research is motivated by the challenge of shaping an **open global economy that fosters innovation and prosperity while addressing climate change and global inequalities**. Working at the intersection of international, environmental and innovation economics, I study how global value chains, foreign investment and industrial policies shape firms' behaviour, environmental performance and technological development. 

My research draws on firm-level data from different countries and applied microeconometric methods, with a growing focus on the global race for technological leadership and the role of industrial policy.



[More about my research →](research.qmd)

:::

## Policy & Public Engagement


My policy work brings an international economics perspective to industrial policy and the green transformation. Through the [Industrial Policy Lab](https://industrialpolicylab.de/de/start/){.inline-link}, I examine how industrial policies shape technological competition, firms' investment decisions and international production networks. My current work covers the EU Industrial Accelerator Act, including the debate over "Made in Europe" versus "Made with Europe" and requirements on foreign investment, as well as the transformation of energy-intensive industries such as steel and the development of hydrogen technologies. Across these topics, I focus on the implications for decarbonisation, competitiveness and an open global economy.

Over the past decade, I have contributed to research, evaluation and policy projects for *German federal ministries, the European Parliament, UNIDO and GIZ*. I also spent three months as a visiting researcher at the *European Commission's Joint Research Centre* in Seville.

I regularly contribute interviews and commentary on economic policy, industrial transformation and sustainability to *ZDF, ARD tagesschau, Deutschlandfunk, WDR5, NDR, dpa, Table.Media (China.Table) and Tagesspiegel Background*.

## Consultancy & International Projects

Since 2016, I have completed more than 20 assignments and over 500 consulting days as an independent consultant and international expert in development cooperation.

My work for **GIZ, GFA Consulting Group, UNIDO and other partners** covers research, survey design, statistical sampling, monitoring and evaluation, training and quality assurance. I have worked as a team leader, coordinator and trainer, with field experience in Mozambique and Kenya.

::: {.consultancy-points}

- **Evaluation & Survey Design**  
  Designing sampling strategies, data collections and quantitative and qualitative evaluations.

- **Project Leadership & Quality Assurance**  
  Coordinating project teams and data collections while ensuring methodological quality.

- **Training & Local Collaboration**  
  Working with institutions, project teams and local partners to translate evidence into practical recommendations.
